newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech Unipetrol chief favours state selloff - paper.
newsitem.headline: Czech Unipetrol chief favours state selloff - paper.

text.p: Miroslav Tera, chairman of Czech state-owned oil refiner Unipetrol a.s., is in favour of a gradual selloff of the state's stake to foreign investors, economic daily Hospodarske Noviny reported on Tuesday.
"I do not see a reason why the state should hold a long-term stake in Unipetrol," he told the paper in an interview.

Tera said that the firm did not seek a single strategic partner, but instead he favoured the sale of "parcels of Unipetrol shares to several institutional foreign investors". "How the state proceeds is obviously its own business," he said.

As part of a complicated privatisation of the Czech petrochemical industry, the refining operations of Kaucuk a.s. and Chemopetrol Group a.s. were merged into a subsidiary of the newly-created Unipetrol last year called Ceska Rafinerska a.s.
Unipetrol has a 51 percent stake in Ceska Rafinerska.
The IOC consortium -- comprising U.S. Du Pont de Nemours unit Conoco, Royal Dutch/Shell, and Italy's Agip SpA -- acquired a 49 percent stake in Rafinerska under agreement with the government in 1995.
The boards of Kauck and Chemopetrol have agreed to swap one Chemopetrol share for between 1.05 and 1.20 Unipetrol shares, and one Kaucuk share for between 1.10 and 1.25 Unipetrol shares.

The transaction will complete the transfer of the rest of Kaucuk and Chemopetrol as subsidiaries under Unipetrol, which acts as a holding company, and would dilute the state's 100 percent stake in Unipetrol.
